page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with a distinct memory-weighted profile. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, it supplies 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores utilizing hyper-threading. The system allocates 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures for persistence.

Benchmark results place the processor in lower performance brackets across compute-intensive metrics. The CPU achieves a PassMark score of 5197.9 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 4396.19, both aligning with the bottom quartile. Single-threaded throughput also trails modern compute-focused platforms, yielding a Geekbench 6 single-core score of 955.0 and weak compression rates. However, memory subsystems demonstrate stable throughput, registering 28.36 GB/sec in large uncached write operations alongside an average score of 5455.52 in extended CPU instruction evaluations.

Given its hardware distribution, the primary design tradeoff centers on high memory density paired with conservative execution speed. Instances of this tier offer resource cost efficiency when applications demand substantial working memory capacities without generating heavy compute or continuous compilation loads.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is practical for memory-reliant workloads such as caching tiers, Redis instances, staging databases, data aggregation buffers, and mid-tier enterprise enterprise applications requiring elevated RAM allocations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.large is a memory-oriented virtual server running on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 32.0 GB of memory, resulting in an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, with no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks reveal modest single-thread and multi-core computational output, placing raw processor throughput and compression metrics in lower tiers. Memory write bandwidth performs steadily at 28.36 GB/sec, demonstrating adequate capacity for data buffering. The instance delivers cost efficiency primarily by providing significant RAM density rather than peak processing throughput. This profile makes the instance well suited for memory-intensive services such as in-memory caches, light database workloads, data buffering, and general memory-bound backend applications.
